newsitem.title: ITALY: ALPINE SKIING-WIBERG OUT OF WOMEN'S COMBINED.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-WIBERG OUT OF WOMEN'S COMBINED.

text.p: Sweden's Pernilla Wiberg, the world and Olympic combined champion, stumbled out of the event at the Alpine skiing world championships on Thursday.

Wiberg, who has won a gold medal at every world championships or Olympic Games that she has competed in, hooked a gate with her left ski on the first run of the slalom and faces the real prospect of leaving without a medal.
Saturday's regular downhill, assuming it goes ahead and is not disrupted by bad weather, is her last hope.
"I haven't been very lucky in these world championships but I have been very lucky in the World Cup," said the overall World Cup leader, who has been fighting a cold here.

Italy's Morena Gallizio, fourth in the 1994 Olympic combined, was the leader after the first leg in a time of 44.13 seconds, ahead of Switzerland's Marlies Oester in 44.47 and Germany's Hilde Gerg in 45.31.
Gallizio and Oester were the first two starters.

The combined slalom, held under floodlights in steadily-falling snow, had been scheduled to follow the downhill race in the afternoon. But that race was called off due to strong winds and re-scheduled for Friday morning.
Only 23 competitors entered the slalom and Wiberg, winner of the last combined held in Laax, Switzerland, this month, was one of two non-finishers in the 53-gate run down the Kandahar piste.
The other was Norway's Ingeborg Helen Marken.

"I will try to laugh about it," said Wiberg of her misfortune. She confirmed that she would compete in Saturday's downhill but did not rate her chances very highly in a discipline that she has never before won.
"(Germany's Katja) Seizinger, (Swiss Heidi) Zurbriggen and (Italy's Isolde) Kostner were all very good in training.

Seizinger and Austria's Anita Wachter, with Gerg the favourites in Wiberg's absence, clocked 45.86 and 46.63 respectively to take fifth and eighth places after the opening run. The second leg was scheduled for 2000 GMT.
Wiberg said her goal now was to win the overall World Cup to go to the 1998 Nagano Olympics as the champion.
